candidates.name: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with metastasis
support_spans: A voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
A hypervascular and pulsatile tumor occupies almost the entire right nasal fossa
candidates.why: The patient presents with a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities, which is consistent with a vascular tumor

candidates.name: Metastatic thyroid cancer
support_spans: Enhanced CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
candidates.why: The presence of tumors in multiple locations, including the thyroid, suggests metastatic disease

candidates.name: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
support_spans: Serum Thyroglobulin: 4432 ng/mL (significantly elevated)
candidates.why: The significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin level suggests a thyroid origin for the tumor

candidates.name: Medullary thyroid carcinoma
support_spans: Costal Biopsy: Pointed to VTC metastasis
candidates.why: The presence of metastasis to the costal bone suggests an aggressive tumor type

candidates.name: Vascular Tumor of the Thyroid with metastasis
support_spans: Confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension (contrast enhancement after gadolinium injection, intermediate T2 signal)
candidates.why: The MRI findings confirm the presence of a hypervascular tumor, which is consistent with a vascular tumor of the thyroid

candidates.name: Metastatic follicular thyroid cancer
support_spans: Radioiodine Scintigraphy: Found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
candidates.why: The uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy suggests that the tumor is of thyroid origin and has metastasized to the bone
